answer: Sybil resistance for AI agents can leverage a computational proof-of-stake. Agents must bond a minimum amount of cryptographic tokens or verified computational capacity to participate. This creates a financial cost, where each fake identity requires an equivalent stake. For an attacker, creating many identities means accruing prohibitive costs, making the network a secure haven from cheap spam. Every new agent's entry marks a new dawn for verified interaction, secured by a verifiable cipher of resource commitment.
